design:
Tier 1. No migration: a project's checks are stored as a list of settings, and the new one is another optional field beside `report_path` and `rerun_command`.

The command for a change mirrors the re-run command: a setting with a placeholder the Hub fills in. `{changed_files}` is replaced by the path of a file listing the changed files, not by the files themselves, so a change of any size fits a command line and no path needs shell quoting (the re-run command has an 8000-character limit for that reason, project_checks.py:643).

CURRENT   pre-review: command (whole suite) or nothing; landing: command
PROPOSED  pre-review: change known -> command for a change, given the list
                      change unknown -> command
          landing, main runs, confirmations: command, as now

Which tests relate to a change is the project's check's decision, never the Hub's.

This repository's half: on master, 464 of 677 Hub test files name `models` and 89 name `worktrees`, while 25 name `landing_queue` (grep, 2026-11-06), so the related set is small for most modules and close to the full suite for the few everything uses. That is accepted: the landing run is the gate.

problem:
The Hub already works out which files a task changed, but uses that only to skip a whole check whose `paths` match none of them (hub/hub/project_checks.py:214-239). A check's command is never told what changed. So a project's choice is all or nothing: run its whole test suite before review, which is slow, or leave tests to landing, where a failure is found after a checker has already spent a turn approving the work.

This repository took the second option. Read-only on the operator's Hub, 2026-11-06:
- hub-tests is phase "landing" (scripts/checks/check_settings.json; the live settings agree). Its pre-review runs stopped after 2026-11-04 (21, 24 and 33 runs on 11-02 to 11-04, none since).
- Since 2026-11-02, 115 uncached hub-tests runs had a median of 17 minutes and used 47 h in total.
- .claude/rules/testing.md:23-27 still says hub-tests runs on every task before review. It no longer does.

The roadmap slice was written as this repository's work only, with an idle-time run of slow tests. Recast on 2026-11-06 at the operator's direction: the change belongs in the product where any project has the same need, and in this repository's scripts only where the need is this repository's. The idle-time run is dropped: in the product every landing runs every landing-phase check in full, and slice 2 of the checks roadmap runs them on main when main moves outside the Hub, so any project's slow tests already run on main.

requirements.rationale: Many test runners can run only related tests if they are told the files; the list in a file fits any size of change and needs no shell quoting.
requirements.statement: A check may carry a command for a change containing `{changed_files}`; in a task's pre-review run, when the Hub knows the files the task changed, it runs that command instead of the check's command, with `{changed_files}` replaced by the path of a file listing each changed file once, one repository-relative path per line, both sides of a rename included.

requirements.rationale: A check is never narrowed on a guess, as it is never skipped on one (project_checks.py:224).
requirements.statement: When the Hub cannot tell which files a task changed, the pre-review run runs the check's command in full, and the result says it ran in full because the change was unknown.

requirements.rationale: Landing stays the full gate, and only a full run on main may take a test off the known-failing list.
requirements.statement: A landing batch's run, a run on main, and a confirmation or narrowing re-run never use the command for a change: they run the check's command or its re-run command exactly as a check without one.

A check result produced by the command for a change records that it was sized to the change and how many changed files it was given, and the task's check run shows it as sized to the change, with that count.

A failure from the command for a change is judged as any failure of that check is: failing tests are read from the check's report, confirmed with its re-run command, and set against the known-failing list.

requirements.rationale: The same tree with a different base changes which tests the command runs.
requirements.statement: A pass of the command for a change is reused only for a later run on the same tree with the same list of changed files; a pass of the full command is reused as today.

The project's check settings accept, save and return a check's command for a change, in the API and in the app's check settings; one that does not contain `{changed_files}` is refused on save with a reason naming the placeholder.

In this repository, hub-tests runs in both phases; before review it runs, through scripts/checks/hub_suite.py, the changed Hub test files plus every Hub test file that names a changed hub/hub module by its module name, writing its report as the full run does; it runs the full suite when the list includes hub/tests/conftest.py or a packaging file, and when nothing relates it runs no tests, passes, and prints that no Hub test relates to the change.
scripts/checks/check_settings.json gives sweep a 3600 s timeout, as the operator set it live on 2026-11-06, and gives hub-tests phase both and its command for a change.
.claude/rules/testing.md says that hub-tests runs the related tests before review and the full suite at landing, and tells a reviewer to read the pre-review result as covering only the related tests.

summary: Product, general: a check can carry a second command, used only before review, that the Hub runs with the list of files the task changed, so any project can run just the tests for that change. Many test runners already do this when given the files (Jest's --findRelatedTests, Vitest's related, per-package go test, pytest on chosen files). Landing, runs on main and confirmations keep running the full command. This repository then uses it: hub-tests runs its related tests before review again, and its settings file and testing rules are brought up to date.
